title: LEAP India Ltd - 544865 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: LEAP India Q1 FY27 total income rose 19% to INR2,134 million, EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million at a 53.5% margin.
summary.overview: LEAP India, India's largest on-demand pallet pooling company, reported its maiden post-listing quarter with total income up 19% YoY to INR2,134 million and EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million. PAT rose 30% to INR247 million (12% margin) and cash PAT rose 23% to about INR812 million. Management reported 48 new customers in the quarter against a normal 15-20, asset count of 14.9 million, and utilisation up to 89.2%. Capex slowed to INR76 million-equivalent (stated as INR76 crores) from INR110 crores a year earlier as raw-material inflation made new crate and pallet purchases less attractive.

financial_highlights.change: up 1.26 million vs Q1 FY26 (13.65 million)
vs INR1.45 in same quarter last year

segments.name: Pallets (pooling)
segments.commentary: Pooled pallet count at around 9.2 million; management targets about 850,000 net additions in FY27 and says pooling growth of 17-18% YoY is achievable. Price increases of 5-6% were taken, linked to the German wood price index.

segments.name: Containers / crates
segments.commentary: Revenue growth of about 13% with asset additions of only 3-4%; management is deliberately slowing crate purchases because crate cost rose from about INR650 to INR1,000-1,200.

segments.name: MHE (TARON)
segments.commentary: 174 new machines added in Q1 and INR35.3 crores revenue (+33%); average monthly MHE pooling turnover rose from INR9.6 crores to INR11.6 crores. Management expects TARON to stay in a 14-17% growth bracket long-term.

segments.name: Middle East (GCC)
segments.commentary: Entities set up in Saudi Arabia (MISA licence), ADGM and Dubai; about five staff and about 20 customer discussions; Q1 capex in the region was held back due to the conflict. Management sees INR150-200 crores revenue in three years.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to about 20% YoY revenue growth (confirmed on the call as YoY, not QoQ), with GCC treated as additive to India growth.
EBITDA margin expected to stay within 47-56% for the next couple of quarters; management sees 100-200 bps potential margin expansion over time, but not a steady quarterly rise.
EBITDA growth expected to exceed revenue growth on a full-year basis, per management's answer to an analyst.
Target of about 3.7 million Movement Hire pallet moves in FY27, with 800,000-900,000 pallets added to the pooling model.
DSO expected to fall 10-15 days per quarter, with working capital normalising within two to three quarters.
Two more warehouses (about 250,000-300,000 sq ft) to be closed in Q2-Q3; a small 40,000-pallet pool may open in Silvassa.
Acquisition opportunities in India and abroad are at an early stage; management indicated updates in Q2-Q3.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 asset spend about INR76 crores vs INR110 crores in Q1 FY26; management is slowing purchases given input cost inflation and is repairing more (1.4 million pallets repaired in Q1 vs 1.2 million a year earlier).
Utilisation target: above 90-91% in the next quarter and 92%+ over the next couple of years; a buffer of about 900,000 pallets is available.
Movement Hire fleet of 400-plus lithium-ion battery forklifts and 140 machines ready for delivery; 1,440 forklifts in total.
Planned 3D printing for inserts and automated crate cleaning by next quarter.
Warehouse network reduced to 28 fulfilment centres after the CHEP integration; 10,500 touchpoints.
demand_pricing: 48 new customers in Q1 (normal run-rate 15-20), including Lear Automotive, Minda Instruments, Havells Logistics, Woodpecker, Green Agri and Sriram Foods; expected to add about 120,000 static-hire pallets.
Beverage and cola demand was extended by a late rainy season (Adhik Maas), shifting demand from March into April-May; this drove positive net pallet additions in Q1.
E-commerce and quick-commerce added about 25,000 pallets (Zomato, Blinkit) and 3PLs added about 30,000 (DP World, DHL, Yusen).
Textile was subdued due to raw-material shortages and cost increases; this reduced Movement Hire volumes.
Pricing: 5-6% annual price increases, linked to the German wood price index, are embedded in 3-5 year contracts; 24 contracts were renewed in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Asset growth was 9% but revenue rose 19%; how is the growth split between asset growth and throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth comes from churn; FY26 moved about 2.8 million pallets and FY27 is targeted at about 3.7 million. Movement Hire rose 8% and textile/other sectors contributed the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide to EBITDA margins for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have ranged 47-56% over six to seven years; FY26 was 50.7% and Q1 was 53.5%. Management expects 47-56% for the next couple of quarters and does not expect steady quarterly expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ revenue growth on a YoY basis and is Middle East additive?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed YoY. Middle East is additive. Management expects INR150-200 crores of GCC revenue in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is container revenue growth modest at 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: No slowdown in demand; management is limiting purchases because crate costs rose sharply, and is retrieving existing assets faster.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pallet 'sales' revenue look up about 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sells pallets only selectively, to customers who will eventually return to pooling; it says this is not a core focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue uplift from static to Movement Hire?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-pallet yield is INR1.54 (about INR562 a year). Management says it could rise to INR600-712 as Movement Hire share increases from about 0.3x toward 0.5-0.6x, with no new assets needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Movement Hire only 0.3x in India and what would lift it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a fragmented truck market (about 1,000 body sizes) and recommended standardising to about 10. It said that when one large player adopts pooling, peers follow.

risks_watch: Middle East (GCC) ramp-up is delayed by the regional conflict; first pooling go-live slipped to mid-September after August intensification, and management says it has other levers within India to cover any shortfall.

Input-cost inflation in crates and timber: management is slowing crate purchases (INR76 crores vs INR110 crores), which could weigh on container asset growth and pallet additions if costs stay elevated.
Movement Hire growth of 8% lagged asset and revenue growth, with textile subdued by raw-material shortages; the FY27 target of about 3.7 million moves needs a sharp pickup in the back half.

Margin path: management guided EBITDA margin of 47-56% for the next couple of quarters and said quarterly expansion will not be steady, while also saying EBITDA growth will outpace 20%+ revenue growth; monitor how these reconcile as MHE mix rises.
Working capital: DSO fell to 119 days from 131 days; management expects 10-15 days reduction per quarter, with normalisation in two to three quarters. Track delivery against this.

Acquisitions are at an early stage in India and abroad; management indicated updates in Q2-Q3. Also watch related-party transaction commentary raised in the market, which management addressed on the call.

summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pooling growth, pricing and customer wins, with stated targets on 20%+ growth and 800,000-900,000 net pallet additions. Cautious on the Middle East (capex held back, go-live delayed) and on crate and container investment given input-cost inflation, and noncommittal on quarterly margin direction, which management said will not rise steadily.

growth.why: Management guides 20%+ YoY revenue growth for FY27 backed by 850,000 net pallet additions (~9% of 9.2M pooled pallets), 48 new customers vs 15-20 normal, and utilisation rising to 89.2% with 90-91% targeted next quarter; partly offset by capex cut to INR76 crore from INR110 crore and slowed crate purchases.
